result:
Admins can now change a user's role from the users list. The row's select sends `PATCH /users/{userId}/role`, the list refetches so the new role shows, and a "User Role Updated" success notification appears. I didn't run tests, lint or the app, as you asked, so this is checked by reading only.

Changes, all in `apps/react-vite`:

- **`src/features/users/api/update-user-role.ts`** (new): a Zod `userRoleSchema` (`ADMIN` | `USER`), the `updateUserRole` fetcher, and `useUpdateUserRole`. The hook invalidates the users query and adds the success notification. I put the notification here because the new `features/CLAUDE.md` rule asks for that.
- **`src/features/users/components/update-user-role.tsx`** (new): a native `<select>` in each row, disabled while the mutation is pending.
- **`src/features/users/components/users-list.tsx`**: the Role column now renders `UpdateUserRole` instead of plain text.
- **`src/testing/mocks/handlers/users.ts`**: a MSW `PATCH /users/:userId/role` handler. It requires auth and admin, rejects roles other than `ADMIN` or `USER` with 400, scopes the update to the admin's team, and persists the change.

Choices I made that you may want to change:

- The signed-in admin's own row shows the role as plain text, not a select. This mirrors how the delete button is hidden on your own row and avoids accidentally demoting yourself.
- `delete-user.tsx` still shows its success notification from the component, which goes against the new rule. I left it alone because it's outside this task.
- The app only has MSW mocks, so the real backend endpoint is assumed to match `PATCH /users/{userId}/role` with a `{ role }` body.

I did not commit anything.
